ansi_slas_standard.name: ANSI/SLAS 1-2004 (R2012) Footprint, ANSI/SLAS 2-2004 Height, ANSI/SLAS 3-2004 Bottom Outside Flange, ANSI/SLAS 4-2004 Well Positions (formerly ANSI/SBS 1-4-2004); ANSI/SLAS 6-2012 Well Bottom Elevation (definitions only)
ansi_slas_standard.material: Not specified by the standards (dimensional standards only).

mass_g.note: Standards do not specify mass.

ansi_slas_standard.grasp_notes: Both footprint sides exceed the PiPER's 70 mm jaw opening (85.48 x 127.76 mm at the flange; the body above the flange is only ~1-2 mm/side smaller, e.g. Eppendorf 96/F 83.1 mm wide), so no standard two-finger side grip is possible with stock fingers. Workable options: (1) custom wide-span fingers with each pad offset outward >=15 mm so the 0-70 mm stroke maps to ~30-100 mm, gripping across the 85.5 mm width on the vertical body wall above the flange (Opentrons Flex grips Corning 96 at 12.2 mm above the base; cross-check only); (2) a 3D-printed SBS carrier/tray with a <=40 mm wide handle tab the stock fingers can pinch; (3) a fork/spatula end-effector that slides under the plate from a raised nest (plate-hotel style). Avoid pinching only one skirt wall (cantilevered, spill risk). Mass is negligible vs the 1.5 kg payload. For nests: pocket ~128.5 x 86.3 mm with lead-in chamfers; pocket inside-corner radius <=1.5 mm (plate corner radius can be as small as 1.58 mm) or add corner reliefs.
ansi_slas_standard.notes: All values quoted from the slas.org PDFs (dated 10/12-10/13/2011). Dimensions apply at 20 C and do NOT include draft. Footprint is measured at the base (bottom flange), must be continuous and uninterrupted; +/-0.25 applies within 12.7 mm of each corner, +/-0.5 elsewhere along a side. Corner radius applies to the four outside corners of the bottom flange (1.58-4.78 mm allowed). SLAS-2 has two compliance parts: 4.1 adds a >=1 mm clearance under the wells, 4.2 does not. SLAS-3 has five classes (short 2.41, medium 6.10, tall 7.62, short with a single centred interruption per long side <=6.85 tall, dual 2.41/7.62); flange width >=1.27 mm; chamfers (corner notches) are optional in quantity/location but must not include the flange, i.e. the flange footprint stays a full rounded rectangle while the body above it may be notched (usually at A1). SLAS-4: A1 is top-left with the plate in landscape, A1 row nearest the 'top' long edge; top-left well must be marked. last_*_center values are derived (A1 offset + (n-1) x pitch) and show the layout is centred. In a front-left-bottom origin frame (Opentrons convention) A1 centre y = 85.48 - 11.24 = 74.24 (96) and 85.48 - 8.99 = 76.49 (384). SLAS-6 defines well-bottom elevation terms and a measurement method but sets no numeric value.

plate_lid_sbs.grasp_notes: 127 x 85 mm also exceeds the 70 mm jaw opening. The lid only rests on the plate, so lifting a plate by its lid lifts the lid alone; when gripping a lidded plate by its sides you squeeze the lid skirt onto the plate body. Low-profile lids (Greiner 656190/191) are designed so a covered plate can still be gripped on its side. Lid-on stacking adds ~3.5 mm to plate height (14.22 -> ~17.7 mm).

Greiner 'high profile (9 mm)' comes from a distributor listing (Greiner's own PDS only says high/low profile). Overlap, plate+lid height (14.22 - 6.5 + 10) and lid stack pitch (10 - 1) are derived from the Opentrons Corning lid definition (cross-check only, rounded 127 x 85 x 10). Model as a 1.2 mm top plate with a perimeter skirt of ~1 mm wall whose inside clears the plate body (~125 x 83 mm) with ~0.5-1 mm gap, a 45-deg corner notch at A1, and (for condensation-ring lids) 96 small rings on the underside on the 9 mm SLAS grid centred over the wells. petri_dish_90mm.grasp_notes: Does NOT fit across the 70 mm jaws (base OD 87.9, lid OD 92.4). The 16 mm closed thickness fits easily, so grasp the rim edge-on: (a) park the dish on a pedestal of ~60-70 mm diameter so 10-15 mm of rim overhangs, then pinch lid+base together vertically at the overhang (keeps the lid on); (b) store dishes on edge in a slotted rack and pinch the 16 mm thickness; (c) a suction cup on the base is the usual alternative. Never lift by the lid alone - it rests loose on vent ribs and will separate. Inverted (agar-down) dishes are normal; the base then sits on top. Smooth PS is slippery and static-prone: rubber finger pads help. Filled mass ~40 g is trivial vs 1.5 kg payload.
petri_dish_90mm.notes: No single maker publishes all dims, so this is a composite of equivalent dishes: lid OD/height, base ID and inner depth from SPL 10090 (90 x 15 mm); base OD 87.91 from Corning's spec for Falcon 351029 ("O.D.", interpreted as base OD because its 56.5 cm2 growth area implies ~84.8 mm ID); closed height 16.1 mm (101VR20, 3 vents) / 15.9 mm (101R20, 1 vent) from Thermo. The US "100 x 15 mm" dish (Falcon 351029, 3 vents, stackable) is the same size class as the European 90 mm dish (growth area 56.5 vs 57.5 cm2); a US lab most likely has 100 x 15 dishes. Thermo cites EN ISO 24998:2008 dimensional controls; Thermo's "Height (English) 16.1 in." is a typo for mm. Estimated values: base_height = closed height - lid top - vent gap; wall ~0.9 mm is consistent with (87.91 - 85.9)/2 and with the 16 g mass. Modelling: base = shallow cup with ~1 deg draft and a low foot/stacking ring under the floor; lid = inverted cup whose skirt clears the base OD by ~1.3 mm/side, with 3 internal vent ribs (0.5-0.7 mm) at 120 deg holding it off the base rim; fillet edges 0.3-0.5 mm.

weigh_boat.grasp_notes: Most likely in a small lab: MEDIUM (hex 02-202-101, 67 mm inner top, or the ~85-89 mm "3.5 in" square). Small (36 mm) fits the jaws; medium hex is at the 70 mm limit and the square medium/large exceed it, so do not grasp across the boat. Walls are ~0.25 mm and collapse under jaw force (useful for pouring, bad for pick-up): pinch one straight rim/side wall with the jaws closing vertically at the lip, or better, sit the boat in a 3D-printed carrier/tray with a grip tab and move the carrier. An empty 1.4 g boat is blown around by airflow and clings to fingers by static - use antistatic boats, an ionizer, or a weight in the carrier. Keep fingers out of the sample.
weigh_boat.notes: Fisher lists hex boats by "Diameter (Metric) Inner Top/Inner Base" - not stated whether across flats or corners; assume across flats (corner-to-corner = 1.155x). Sloping sides with a 4.8 mm (0.187 in) inside corner radius. Hex capacities are computed as hexagonal frustums (7.5/42.6/182 mL); Heathrow's hexagonal boats of near-identical size list 6/46/194/364 mL (small/medium/large/x-large), so those are a good cross-check. Wall thickness is derived from the Fisher masses and the frustum surface area (0.22-0.30 mm, PS 1.05 g/cm3). Heathrow square boats: sizes are L x W x H as listed (1.8x1.8x0.3 in, 3.4x3.4x0.9 in, 5.5x5.5x0.9 in); bottom L/W is estimated at ~0.7x top (Fisher hex bottom/top = 0.67-0.77). Dyn-A-Med 80055 dims from inches 3.31 x 3.31 x 0.75 in. Modelling: a hexagonal or square frustum shell, ~30-35 deg wall slope from vertical, 4.8 mm inside corner fillets, flat bottom, optional 1 mm flat lip.

sem_stub_pin_12p7mm.name: SEM pin stub, Ø12.7 mm (1/2") aluminium, standard 3.2 mm pin (Ted Pella PELCO 16111 [8 mm pin] / 16111-9 [ZEISS 6 mm pin]; EMS 75200/75210/75220/75230; Agar G301 [8 mm] / G301F [6 mm]; EM-Tec 10-002012)

groove.profile: shallow rectangular/V ring groove on head OD for tweezers/grippers

pin.tip_style: tapered/chamfered end on standard (Cambridge/FEI) stubs; flat end on ZEISS 75500-series and Ted Pella 16202

sem_stub_pin_12p7mm.material: Vacuum-grade / free-cutting or ultra-pure aluminium, bright silver lathe (standard) or cloth-polished (luster) finish; also sold in brass, copper, stainless steel and high-purity carbon

mass_g.note: ESTIMATE from geometry x 2.70 g/cm3: 1.17 g (6 mm pin), 1.21 g (8 mm pin), 1.24 g (9.5 mm pin). Filled = stub + 12 mm carbon tab (~0.02 g) + typical small sample (0.05-0.5 g); a vendor web-shop weight of 0.118 lb per pack of 100 (~0.54 g each) is inconsistent with this geometry and was not used.

sem_stub_pin_12p7mm.grasp_notes: Fits easily (12.7 mm << 70 mm opening) but is tiny and ~1.2 g, so jaw closing accuracy dominates. Grip the head rim/groove (the groove exists for tweezers and PELCO SEM-mount grippers) with custom fingertips: a V-notch or 12.9 mm semicircular pocket, jaws approaching horizontally. Never touch the top face (sample, carbon tab) and do not grip the pin (poor torque resistance, and it must stay clean to seat in stage/box holes). Insertion into a box or stage hole needs about +/-0.3 mm lateral accuracy for a 3.15 mm pin in a ~3.2 mm hole; add a chamfered lead-in or wrist compliance. LDPE box inserts grip the pin by friction, so extraction must be a straight vertical pull. An alternative is to move a multi-stub holder instead of single stubs.
sem_stub_pin_12p7mm.notes: PIN-LENGTH FAMILIES (the premise 'Zeiss long pin' is inverted): the standard FEI/Thermo/TESCAN/Cambridge/Philips stub has an 8 mm pin (Ted Pella 16111 'x 8mm pin height'; Agar G301 'pin length 8 mm'; EMS numbered 75220-12 'Pin Height: 8mm'), but many vendors make 9-9.5 mm (3/8") pins (Ted Pella divided mounts '9mm (3/8") long'; Ted Pella starter kit 76250-10 '9mm long pin mounts'; EMS divided 75183-series 'Pin Height: 9.0 mm'). ZEISS/LEO stages take the SHORT 6 mm pin (Ted Pella 16111-9, Agar G301F, EM-Tec Zeiss range, Ted Pella kit 76260-20 '6mm long pin mounts'). Oddities: Ted Pella 16202 is a 'Special ZEISS/LEO' 9 mm pin with no chamfer on the leg; EMS 75190 is a LEO tapered pin x 5 mm; EMS 75500/75510/75520 is a ZEISS flat-end pin (length not stated). EMS 75200/75210/75220/75230 are one and the same Cambridge-style tapered-pin 1/2" stub in 10/50/100/500 packs, NOT different pin lengths. Agar quotes the same stub as 12.5 mm diameter; Ted Pella/EMS say 12.7 mm (1/2"), so model 12.7. Variants: Ted Pella 16118 has a 7.4 mm tall head; EM-Tec sells +4 mm and +6 mm extra-height heads and 1 mm low-profile heads. In a FEI/TFS stage the pin is clamped by a side set screw, so pin length only limits seating depth. Modelling: revolve a Ø12.7 x 3.2 disc, cut the ring groove, add a Ø3.15 pin with 0.4 x 45 deg tip chamfer. ESTIMATE REASONS: head thickness 3.2 is stated by EM-Tec for flat ZEISS stubs and assumed identical for standard stubs (same head, different pin); groove/edge-break/tip-chamfer sizes are not published; pin Ø3.15 chosen within the 3.1-3.2 catalogue range (1/8" = 3.175); overall heights are head + pin sums. The side-set-screw clamping remark is general SEM practice, not from the cited pages.
